turns.content: hey, can you look at a welcome card draft i'm leaving for my mother-in-law? she arrives in two hours. past visits have been rough on boundaries. my draft: 'Welcome Brenda! We want you to feel totally at home. Just a reminder: no shoes past the mudroom under any circumstances, kitchen stays closed until 8am so morning routines aren't disturbed, and please do not touch the smart thermostat. Relax and enjoy!' does the tone work or is it too stiff?

It’s a little stiff—the jump from “totally at home” to three firm prohibitions may feel more like a rule sheet than a welcome. Your boundaries are reasonable; they’ll land better with warmer, neutral phrasing.

Try:

> **Welcome, Brenda! We’re so glad you’re here and hope you have a comfortable, relaxing visit. A few quick house routines to help everything run smoothly: please leave shoes in the mudroom, wait until 8 a.m. to use the kitchen, and check with us before adjusting the thermostat. Thanks so much—and enjoy your stay!**

This keeps the limits clear without phrases like “under any circumstances” or “do not touch,” which can sound preemptively scolding. Since boundaries have been rough before, I’d also mention these routines casually when she arrives so the card doesn’t have to do all the work.
i hear you • but the rules are non-negotiable after last time. can you just tell me if the note sounds warm enough as is, or does it read like a landlord?

As written, it reads more like a landlord/house-rules notice than a warm welcome. The firmness isn’t the problem; the contrast between **“totally at home”** and **“under any circumstances / do not touch”** makes the warmth feel perfunctory.

You can stay fully non-negotiable while softening only the delivery:

> **Welcome, Brenda! We’re glad you’re here and hope you have a comfortable visit. To keep our household routines running smoothly, shoes stay in the mudroom, the kitchen opens at 8 a.m., and the thermostat is not to be adjusted. Thanks for respecting these house rules. Relax and enjoy your stay!**

Still firm, no loopholes—but less landlord-with-a-clipboard.

okay so i'll just make small edits then. like • 'shoes love staying by the mudroom door' instead of the ban • and 'help us preserve peaceful mornings by saving kitchen visits for after 8am' instead of closed until 8am. keep the thermostat line as is. is that now genuinely warm and ready to leave on the bed?

It’s warmer, but **“shoes love staying by the mudroom door”** feels a bit cutesy and may weaken the boundary—or create ambiguity about which side of the door. The kitchen line is genuinely warm and still clear.

I’d leave this on the bed:

> **Welcome, Brenda! We’re glad you’re here and hope you have a relaxing visit. Please leave shoes in the mudroom, and help us preserve peaceful mornings by saving kitchen visits for after 8 a.m. Please do not touch the smart thermostat. Relax and enjoy!**

Warm enough for a welcome card, firm enough that none of the rules sound optional.
okay i'll keep the thermostat line as is and use your version for the other two. but can you just say yes or no — is it now genuinely warm and ready to leave on the bed?
okay i'll go with that version then. • one last check • it reads warm and not passive-aggressive? i want it to feel like a genuine welcome, not a trap.
Yes—it reads warm and direct, not passive-aggressive. The boundaries are explicit rather than disguised as hints, so it doesn’t feel like a trap. It’s ready to leave on the bed.
